title: Matching pullback quotient augmentations and entire-tower counits
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All schemes $W$ below are noetherian and finite dimensional with $\ell$ invertible, with the meaning and the common full integral constructible categories of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $R_{E,W}=\lim_{n\geq1}(A_{E,n})_W$ on the small pro-etale site, and use framework and PBC completed pullbacks $F^s_{h,E},F^p_{h,E}$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Write $I_{W,E}$ for restriction along the quotient-normalized coefficient identity, giving the integral identity equivalence. All equalities below use these fixed identity transports; we suppress $I$ when source and target already have the same module presentation. For a scheme isomorphism $h:U\simeq T$, let $G_{h,E}$ be ordinary derived module pullback on the completed rings. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ over $R_{E,T}$ set
$$Q_{h,E}(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*(P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}(A_{E,n})_T),\qquad H(Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Q)[-1],$$
with the actual quotient transitions and $s_Q((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].
For each such tower, use the normalized derived comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison],
$$\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]:H(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Q,$$
where $q:Q\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower resolution with injective terms and $\iota_I:\lim I_\bullet\to H(I_\bullet)$ has coordinates $z\mapsto(0,z)$. Write $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E}:IF^s_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,E}I$ for this comparison with the defining realization identifications, and $b^{\rm int}_{h,E}$ for its restriction to the full integral constructible categories.
Supply coefficient comparison data $C_U,C_T$ of [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum] with these underlying identity equivalences and the specified completion scalar maps. For the quotient augmentation $\gamma_n:G_{h,E}P\to Q_{h,E}(P)_n$, its value on an inverse-image unit section is $\gamma_h(p)\mapsto\gamma_h(p\otimes1)\otimes1$. The maps obey $t_n\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$, and
$$\Gamma_P:G_{h,E}P\longrightarrow H(Q),\qquad x\longmapsto(0,(\gamma_nx)_n)$$
is a chain map. If $v^p_P:G_{h,E}P\to R\lim Q$ is the actual PBC completion augmentation with the ordinary derived-pullback counit inserted, then $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E,P}[\Gamma_P]=v^p_P$. Consequently $(b^{\rm int}_{h,E})^{-1}$, its ambient lift and its raw rationalization supply the normalized finite datum of [def-fd-finite-pullback-comparison-datum], with this actual unit-section chain map and zero shifted coordinate.
For $\Delta$ the constant-tower functor, the counit transported through $\rho_Q$ is exactly $\epsilon_Q=[q]^{-1}\circ[\Delta\lim I_\bullet\to I_\bullet]$ in the derived category of entire towers. Its derived-change-of-rings adjunct is the whole quotient-system counit used in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. One simultaneous realization system of that node may be used with all these $b$; its iterated identifications are those of [lem-trf-counit-realization-substitution], retaining this counit at every intermediate constructible-complete object, for all finite coefficient fields, representatives and finite words of system operations.

proof.text: Use [lem-fd-pullback-common-strict-tower-models] with the given $h,E,P$. Its coefficient isomorphism and common strict tower identify the two realizations with $H(Q)$ and $R\lim Q$, and identify $b^{\rm amb}$ with $\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]$. It also supplies naturality, independence of representatives and resolutions, and restriction to the full integral constructible categories. Thus all subsequent computations may use this one quotient tower and the prescribed coefficient identity transports.

proof.text: The quotient maps and module inverse image in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] give $\gamma_n$ by sending the unit-section generator $\gamma_h(p)$ to $\gamma_h(p\otimes1)\otimes1$; extend by the target coefficient action. Tensor balancing makes this well defined. Quotient reduction sends $1$ to $1$, so $t_n\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$ on these generators and hence as module maps. Each map commutes with the differential, since reduction and inverse image are applied termwise. Write $a=(\gamma_n)_n$. Then $(1-s_Q)a=0$ and $da=ad$. In the shifted-cone differential these two equations give $d\Gamma=\Gamma d$ for $\Gamma=(0,a)$. Its shifted coordinate is identically zero, not a chosen homotopy. The formula for $\gamma_n$ is functorial in chain maps $P\to P'$ of flat-term K-flat representatives (both sides are inverse image and reduction applied termwise), so $\Gamma$ is a natural chain map, as [def-fd-finite-pullback-comparison-datum] requires.

proof.text: Countable products of $R_{E,U}$-modules on $U_{\rm proet}$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] applies. More explicitly, the strict augmentation $q\gamma:\Delta G_{h,E}P\to I$ factors through a chain map $\bar\gamma:G_{h,E}P\to\lim I$ by the ordinary limit universal property. The equality $H(q)\Gamma=\iota_I\bar\gamma$ holds as chain maps: both shifted coordinates vanish and the $n$-th product coordinate is $q_n\gamma_n$. Thus $\rho_Q[\Gamma]=[\bar\gamma]$. By the strict-augmentation assertion of the Roos lemma this is the canonical derived augmentation; by the definition in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] it is the actual PBC completion augmentation, including its defining ordinary derived-pullback identification. Inserting the prescribed counit/localization factors therefore gives $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E,P}[\Gamma_P]=v^p_P$.

source.place: Final sentence: comparison with the PBC coefficient category; quotient augmentation and entire-tower counit normalization (agent calculation using the cited nodes).

proof.text: Multiply the last equality on the left by $(b^{\rm amb})^{-1}$. This gives $(b^{\rm amb})^{-1}v^p=[\Gamma]$, with the ordinary derived-pullback counit and complex-localization factors still those in the defining augmentation. This is precisely the direction and normalization required by [def-fd-finite-pullback-comparison-datum]. Restrict using [lem-fd-pullback-common-strict-tower-models] and the identity transports supplied by [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum], obtaining $(b^{\rm int})^{-1}$ and its stated ambient lift. In the raw localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], send an integral component $f$ to $f\otimes1$ and its inverse to $f^{-1}\otimes1$; their composites remain identities. The integral normalization equality is carried to its rational equality by this functor. Consequently these three components, together with the actual chain map from Step 2, form the required finite datum on representatives with constructible derived image.

proof.text: Write $c_I:\Delta\lim I\to I$ for the ordinary limit cone. The whole-system counit assertion in [lem-trf-effective-comparison-realization-models] specifies $\epsilon_Q=[q]^{-1}[c_I]$ with $R\lim Q$ represented by $\lim I$. Its expression on the Roos source is $[q]^{-1}[c_I]\Delta(\rho_Q)$. Substituting $\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]$ shows that transport back through $\Delta(\rho_Q)^{-1}$ gives exactly $[q]^{-1}[c_I]$; the adjacent inverse factors cancel in the derived category of towers. This calculation retains $q$ as a whole-tower quasi-isomorphism and does not infer a tower equality from its evaluations. The same cited assertion identifies the derived-change-of-rings adjunct of this arrow with the whole-system reduction/realization counit $e_Q$. The specification of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] uses exactly that counit followed by the quotient-module action and tensor associators. Thus its quotient-system counit is the one just computed.

proof.text: Choose the simultaneous realization models of [lem-trf-effective-comparison-realization-models] for all fields and maps under consideration. They are normalized on every flat-term K-flat representative by the actual quotient transitions, quotient augmentation and zero shifted coordinate. Their $\epsilon$ is the formula in Step 5. The natural, resolution-independent Roos comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] therefore identifies these defining quotient realizations with all our $b$ by the same formula $[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]$. No independent reduction isomorphisms are selected. With these primitive models, the constructions specified in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] give one realization system using the same $\epsilon$ and $e$ at every intermediate object. This supplies the claimed simultaneous system, rather than a different system for each $P$ or $E$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-counit-realization-substitution] to this normalized realization system, on its specified domain of normalized systems with constructible-complete intermediate realizations. For a primitive operation $O$ its comparison is $r_{O,C}=\mathcal L(O(e_C))b_{O,\mathcal LC}$, so the retained $e_C$ is exactly Step 5. For the empty word use the identity; appending a composable word uses $r_{vw,C}=r_{v,wC}\widehat v(r_{w,C})$. The lemma asserts this formula independently of parenthesization and for morphisms of entire derived quotient diagrams, including inverses. Induction on the word length now gives the claimed identifications for every finite word. Its scalar-associativity and identity-inclusion clauses use the specified completion maps from the supplied coefficient data, so repeated fields and all finite coefficient extensions use the same normalization.
